newsitem.title: USA: Kansas wheat seeding under way, fall crops advance.
newsitem.headline: Kansas wheat seeding under way, fall crops advance.

text.p: Wheat seeding had begun in western Kansas and fall crop progress continued ahead of average pace during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly update.
Three percent of the state's wheat acreage had been seeded, ahead of one percent last year but lagging the average of four percent.

Corn condition was rated 87 percent good to excellent, 10 percent fair and three poor to very poor. Thirty-eight percent of the corn acreage was mature, versus 13 percent last year and the average of 44 percent.

Sorghum condition was rated 87 percent good to excellent, 12 percent fair and one percent poor. The crop was 13 percent mature, ahead of the average of eight percent. There were reports of corn earworms in sorghum fields in central and southern Kansas, but the extent of damage was unknown.
Soybeans were rated 86 percent good to excellent, 13 fair and one percent poor.
Topsoil moisture was rated nine percent short, 87 percent adequate and four percent surplus.
Pasture condition was rated 81 percent good to excellent, 16 percent fair and three percent poor.
